name: CHORD Tables: the stock CHORD machine plays wavetables from the +Drive, RETRIG + SWEEP picks one
description: An extension of the stock CHORD machine (notes/66): on CHORD's tracks, RETRIG + SWEEP = Wavetable, 0 to 64, saved with the sound; 0 is the stock table, 1 to 64 the files /Wavetables/01 to /Wavetables/64 on the +Drive (mono sample files of k x 256 samples, k single-cycle frames, k = 1 to 32), loaded on the screen's tick. A note takes its table when it starts; SWEEP moves through the table's frames as on the stock machine. CHORD at 0, and every other track, plays as on the stock OS.

uses.why: an extension of CHORD, machine 5: no machine of its own, no descriptor, nothing registered
the table, k 30 (notes/66 §2.4, §10): 0 the stock table, 1 to 64 a file; cw_setup reads it from the sound a note plays
CHORD's update gets its two frames through this one call (notes/66 §1.1): without a table the stock function, with one its work on the table's frames
the screen's redraw, about 30 Hz, UI task: the loader reads one file per tick; with SAMPLE, through the tick dispatcher
one file as read and 72 table buffers (64 slots, 8 spare), 2.4 MB (notes/66 §2.2)

emulation.pattern: STANDARD.md §6 in tools/emu/test_chordtables.py part C: instructions per block per voice in the real voice loop, CHORD alone on track 1 (machine defaults, note 60, SWEEP 24), trig in block 1, the note's first block then the mean and maximum of the next 21, minus the loop with every voice muted; this line at Wavetable 0
emulation.note: +22 per block per voice at Wavetable 0, -1 with a table; the emulator does not time memory: a table's frames are read in SDRAM instead of SRAM, about +0.6 to +1.2 points of a block per CHORD voice on a table by notes/27 and 28's estimates

changes: CHORD's tracks: RETRIG + SWEEP edits the Wavetable instead of SWEEP
unchanged: CHORD at Wavetable 0, and every other track

emulation.tool: tools/emu/test_chordtables.py (Unicorn, the OS's own code, notes/66 §14)
emulation.build: alone, with sampler before and after it
